content.topic: Respect others, and you will be respected

modelEssay.title: Respect others, and you will be respected
modelEssay.content:
Respect is a fundamental principle in human interaction, and the saying 'Respect others, and you will be respected' encapsulates this idea beautifully. Respecting others means valuing their opinions, acknowledging their feelings, and treating them with dignity. This reciprocal nature of respect is evident in various aspects of life.

For instance, in the workplace, when colleagues respect each other's contributions and ideas, it fosters a positive environment that encourages collaboration and innovation. Similarly, in personal relationships, showing respect for others' boundaries and choices strengthens bonds and builds trust. Moreover, respect is not limited to verbal affirmations; it is also demonstrated through actions, such as listening attentively and being empathetic.

In conclusion, the adage 'Respect others, and you will be respected' is not just a moral guideline but a practical one. It reminds us that respect is a two-way street that enriches our interactions and enhances our social experiences.

transcript.text: And now, for the lighter side of the news, Europe is setting an example for the rest of the world when it comes to food waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 现在，转到新闻的轻松一面，欧洲在食物浪费方面为世界其他地区树立了榜样。

transcript.text: That's right, John.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没错，约翰。

transcript.text: This week, the Italian government passed legislation that aimed to dramatically reduce the amount of food wasted in the country.

transcript.text: New laws have been put into place that will make it easier for farms and supermarkets to donate unsold foods to those who are in need.

transcript.translation: 新法律已经实施，这将使农场和超市更容易将未售出的食物捐赠给有需要的人。

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，除此之外，企业现在将因成功减少食物浪费的努力而获得奖励。

transcript.text: Italy is not the only country to focus on reducing food waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 意大利并不是唯一关注减少食物浪费的国家。

transcript.text: Just earlier this year, the European Parliament voted in favour of legislation that would stop grocery giants from unfair trading practices that result in overproduction, thus creating waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 就在今年早些时候，欧洲议会投票支持了一项立法，该立法将阻止食品巨头进行导致生产过剩从而产生浪费的不公平贸易行为。

transcript.text: In France, the government has banned supermarkets from throwing away edible foods and imposed harsh penalties on businesses that fail to comply with the regulations.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 在法国，政府已禁止超市丢弃可食用食品，并对不遵守规定的企业施加严厉处罚。

transcript.text: While there is still much progress to be made, other countries could learn a thing or two from the example set by France and Italy.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 尽管仍有很大进步空间，其他国家可以从法国和意大利树立的榜样中学到一两件事。

transcript.text: In the United States, up to 40% of all food goes uneaten, despite the fact that one in seven American households lacks regular access to good food.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在美国，高达40%的食物未被食用，尽管每七个美国家庭中就有一个缺乏定期获取优质食物的途径。

transcript.text: One major cause of this problem is the confusion over food expiration labels, which are currently not regulated by the government.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这个问题的一个主要原因是关于食品保质期标签的混淆，这些标签目前不受政府监管。

transcript.text: All this could change soon.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所有这一切可能很快就会改变。

transcript.text: This wave of new laws in Europe will definitely put more pressure on lawmakers to reduce food waste here.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 欧洲的这波新法律无疑将给立法者带来更多压力，以减少这里的食物浪费。

transcript.text: We turn now to a spokesperson from Harvard University's Food Law and Policy Clinic for more on this story.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们现在转向哈佛大学食品法律与政策诊所的发言人，了解更多关于这个故事的信息。

transcript.text: And now, let's welcome Professor Edward Baker to speak to us.

transcript.translation: 现在，让我们欢迎爱德华·贝克教授为我们讲话。

transcript.text: Barbie dolls have a particular look to them.

transcript.text: Her body shape hasn't changed much.

transcript.text: Last year, Mattel, the company that makes Barbie dolls, added some Barbies to its line that have different skin tones and hair textures.
transcript.translation: 去年，制造芭比娃娃的公司美泰在其产品线中增加了一些具有不同肤色和发质的芭比娃娃。

transcript.text: Last year, Mattel also gave Barbie a flat foot, rather than forcing her to be in heels all the time like the original Barbie is.
transcript.translation: 去年，美泰还给芭比娃娃设计了平底脚，而不是像最初的芭比那样一直让她穿高跟鞋。

transcript.text: Now, they are introducing new Barbies with three slightly different body shapes, while the original tall and thin Barbies will continue to be sold.

transcript.text: In a statement on its website, the company says it wants Barbies to look more like real people, and to give girls everywhere infinitely more ways to spark their imagination and play out their stories.

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第二段。

transcript.text: The earliest printed book we know today appeared in China in the year 868, and metal type was in use in Korea at the beginning of the 15th century.
transcript.translation: 我们今天所知的最早的印刷书籍于公元868年出现在中国，而金属活字印刷在15世纪初的韩国已经使用。

transcript.text: But it was in Germany, around the year 1450, that a printing press using movable metal type was invented.
transcript.translation: 但正是在德国，大约在1450年，发明了一种使用可移动金属活字的印刷机。

transcript.text: Capitalism turned printing from an invention into an industry.
transcript.translation: 资本主义将印刷从一项发明转变为一个产业。

transcript.text: Right from the start, book printing and publishing were organised on capitalist lines.
transcript.translation: 从一开始，书籍印刷和出版就是按照资本主义路线组织的。

transcript.text: The biggest 16th century printer, Plantain of Antwerp, had 24 printing presses and employed more than 100 workers.
transcript.translation: 16世纪最大的印刷商，安特卫普的普兰坦，拥有24台印刷机，雇佣了100多名工人。

transcript.text: Only a small fraction of the population was literate, but the production of books grew at an extraordinary speed.
transcript.translation: 只有一小部分人口识字，但书籍生产以惊人的速度增长。

transcript.text: By 1500, some 20 million volumes had already been printed.
transcript.translation: 到1500年，大约2000万卷书籍已经被印刷。

transcript.text: The immediate effect of printing was to increase the circulation of works that were already popular in a handwritten form, while less popular works went out of circulation.
transcript.translation: 印刷的直接效果是增加了那些以手写形式已经流行的作品的流通，而不太流行的作品则退出了流通。

transcript.text: Publishers were interested only in books that would sell fairly quickly in sufficient numbers to cover the costs of production and make a profit.
transcript.translation: 出版商只对那些能以足够数量快速销售、以覆盖生产成本并盈利的书籍感兴趣。

transcript.text: Thus, while printing enormously increased access to books by making cheap, high-volume production possible, it also reduced choice.
transcript.translation: 因此，虽然印刷通过使廉价、高产量的生产成为可能，极大地增加了对书籍的获取，但它也减少了选择。

transcript.text: The great cultural impact of printing was that it facilitated the growth of national languages.
transcript.translation: 印刷的重大文化影响是促进了民族语言的发展。

transcript.text: Most early books were printed in Latin, but the market for Latin was limited, and in its pursuit of larger markets, the book trade soon produced translations into the national languages, emerging at the time.

transcript.text: Kwanzaa is a cultural festival during which African Americans celebrate and reflect upon their rich heritage as the products of two worlds.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节是一个文化节庆，期间非裔美国人庆祝并反思他们作为两个世界产物的丰富遗产。

transcript.text: It begins December 26th and lasts for seven days.
transcript.translation: 它始于12月26日，持续七天。

transcript.text: Kwanzaa was founded in 1966 by Dr.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节由博士于1966年创立。

transcript.text: Karenga, a college professor and African American leader, who believed that a special holiday could help African Americans meet their goals of building strong families, learning about their history, and creating a sense of unity.
transcript.translation: 卡伦加，一位大学教授和非裔美国人领袖，他认为一个特别的节日可以帮助非裔美国人实现他们的目标，即建立稳固的家庭、学习他们的历史并创造团结感。

transcript.text: After conducting extensive research in which he studied the festivals of many African groups of people, he decided that the new holiday should be a harvest or first fruits celebration, incorporating ideas from many different harvest traditions.
transcript.translation: 在进行了广泛研究，学习了许多非洲族群的节庆之后，他决定新节日应是一个丰收或初果庆典，融入了许多不同丰收传统的理念。

transcript.text: Kwanzaa is a Kiswahili word meaning the first fruits of the harvest.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节是一个基斯瓦希里语单词，意为丰收的初果。

transcript.text: The East African language of Kiswahili was chosen as the official language of Kwanzaa because it is a non-tribal language spoken by a large portion of the African population.
transcript.translation: 东非语言基斯瓦希里语被选为宽扎节的官方语言，因为它是一种非部落语言，由大部分非洲人口使用。

transcript.text: Also, its pronunciation is easy.
transcript.translation: 此外，它的发音简单。

transcript.text: Kwanzaa is based on seven principles which are unity, self-determination, collective work and responsibility, cooperative economics, purpose, creativity, and faith.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节基于七个原则，即团结、自决、集体工作和责任、合作经济、目的、创造力和信仰。

transcript.text: One principle is highlighted each day of the holiday.
transcript.translation: 节日的每一天都突出一个原则。

transcript.text: In preparation for the celebration, a straw mat is placed on the table, along with a candle holder with seven candles, one black, three red, and three green.
transcript.translation: 为庆祝做准备，在桌子上放一个草席，旁边是一个有七支蜡烛的烛台，一支黑色、三支红色和三支绿色。

transcript.text: The black candle represents the African American people, the red is for their struggles, and the green represents their hopes for the future.
transcript.translation: 黑色蜡烛代表非裔美国人，红色代表他们的斗争，绿色代表他们对未来的希望。

transcript.text: Other items placed on the table are a variety of fruit, ears of corns, gifts, and a communal unity cup for pouring and sharing drinks.
transcript.translation: 放在桌子上的其他物品有各种水果、玉米穗、礼物和一个用于倒酒和共享饮料的公共团结杯。

transcript.text: Each day of Kwanzaa, usually before the evening meal, family and friends gather around the table and someone lights a candle, beginning with the black.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节的每一天，通常在晚餐前，家人和朋友围坐在桌旁，有人点燃蜡烛，从黑色蜡烛开始。

transcript.text: After that, candles are lit alternately from left to right.
transcript.translation: 之后，蜡烛从左到右交替点燃。

transcript.text: While the candle is being lit, a principle is recited, then each person present takes a turn to speak about the importance that principle has to himself or herself.
transcript.translation: 在点燃蜡烛时，背诵一个原则，然后在场每个人轮流谈论该原则对自己或她自己的重要性。

transcript.text: Next, the ceremony focuses on remembering those who have died.
transcript.translation: 接下来，仪式聚焦于纪念逝者。

transcript.text: A selected person pours water or juice from the unity cup into a bowl.
transcript.translation: 一个被选中的人从团结杯中将水或果汁倒入碗中。

transcript.text: That person then drinks from the cup and raises it high, saying Harambee, which means let's all pour together.
transcript.translation: 然后那个人从杯子中喝一口，并高高举起，说'哈兰比'，意思是让我们一起倒。

transcript.text: All repeat Harambee seven times, and each person drinks from the cup.
transcript.translation: 所有人重复'哈兰比'七次，每个人都从杯子中喝一口。

transcript.text: Then, names of African American leaders and heroes are called out, and everyone reflects upon the great things these people did.
transcript.translation: 然后，喊出非裔美国人领袖和英雄的名字，每个人反思这些人所做的伟大事情。

transcript.text: The ceremony is followed by a meal, and then singing and perhaps listening to African music.
transcript.translation: 仪式之后是餐食，然后是唱歌，或许还听非洲音乐。

transcript.text: The Mediterranean diet is based upon the eating patterns of traditional cultures in the Mediterranean region.
transcript.translation: 地中海饮食是基于地中海地区传统文化的饮食模式。

transcript.text: Several noted nutritionists and research projects have concluded that this diet is one of the most healthful in the world in terms of preventing such illnesses as heart disease and cancer, and increasing life expectancy.
transcript.translation: 几位著名营养学家和研究项目得出结论，这种饮食在预防心脏病和癌症等疾病以及提高预期寿命方面，是世界上最健康的饮食之一。

transcript.text: The countries that have inspired the Mediterranean diet all surround the Mediterranean Sea.
transcript.translation: 启发了地中海饮食的国家都环绕地中海。

transcript.text: These cultures have eating habits that developed over thousands of years.
transcript.translation: 这些文化拥有发展了数千年的饮食习惯。

transcript.text: In Europe, parts of Italy, Greece, Portugal, Spain, and southern France adhere to principles of the Mediterranean diet, as do Morocco and Tunisia in North Africa.
transcript.translation: 在欧洲，意大利、希腊、葡萄牙、西班牙和法国南部的部分地区遵循地中海饮食的原则，北非的摩洛哥和突尼斯也是如此。

transcript.text: Parts of the Balkan region and Turkey follow the diet, as well as Middle Eastern countries like Lebanon and Syria.
transcript.translation: 巴尔干地区和土耳其的部分地区也遵循这种饮食，中东国家如黎巴嫩和叙利亚也是如此。

transcript.text: The Mediterranean region is warm and sunny, and produces large supplies of fresh fruits and vegetables almost year-round that people eat many times a day.
transcript.translation: 地中海地区温暖阳光充足，几乎全年都能生产大量新鲜水果和蔬菜，人们每天多次食用。

transcript.text: Wine, bread, olive oil, and nuts are other staples of the region, and the Mediterranean Sea has historically yielded abundant quantities of fish.
transcript.translation: 葡萄酒、面包、橄榄油和坚果是该地区的其他主食，地中海历史上盛产丰富的鱼类。

transcript.text: International interest in the therapeutic qualities of the Mediterranean diet began back in the late 1950s, when medical researchers started to link the occurrence of heart disease with diet.
transcript.translation: 国际上对地中海饮食治疗特性的兴趣始于20世纪50年代末，当时医学研究人员开始将心脏病的发生与饮食联系起来。

transcript.text: Dr.
transcript.translation: 博士

transcript.text: Ancel Keys performed an epidemiological analysis of diets around the world.
transcript.translation: 安塞尔·凯斯对世界各地的饮食进行了流行病学分析。

transcript.text: Entitled The Seven-Country Study, it is considered one of the greatest studies of its kind ever performed.
transcript.translation: 这项名为《七国研究》的研究被认为是同类研究中最伟大的之一。

transcript.text: In it, Keys gathered data on heart disease and its potential causes from nearly 13,000 men in Greece, Italy, Croatia, Serbia, Japan, Finland, the Netherlands, and the United States.
transcript.translation: 在研究中，凯斯从希腊、意大利、克罗地亚、塞尔维亚、日本、芬兰、荷兰和美国的近13,000名男性中收集了心脏病及其潜在原因的数据。

transcript.text: The study was conducted over a period of decades.
transcript.translation: 这项研究持续了数十年。

transcript.text: It concluded that the Mediterranean people in the study enjoyed some significant health advantages.
transcript.translation: 研究得出结论，参与研究的地中海人群享有显著的健康优势。

transcript.text: The Mediterranean groups had lower mortality rates in all age brackets and from all causes, particularly from heart disease.
transcript.translation: 地中海组在所有年龄段和所有原因（尤其是心脏病）的死亡率都较低。

transcript.text: The study also showed that the Mediterranean diet is as high or higher in fat than other diets, obtaining up to 40% of all its calories from fat.
transcript.translation: 研究还表明，地中海饮食的脂肪含量与其他饮食相当或更高，高达40%的热量来自脂肪。

questionGroups.title: Who's Really Addicting You to Technology?

material.title: Who's Really Addicting You to Technology?

paragraphs.text: "Nearly everyone I know is addicted in some measure to the Internet," wrote Tony Schwartz in The New York Times. It's a common complaint these days. A steady stream of similar headlines accuse the Net and its offspring apps, social media sites and online games of addicting us to distraction.
paragraphs.translation: 托尼·施瓦茨在《纽约时报》中写道：“几乎我认识的每个人都在一定程度上沉迷于互联网。”这是当今常见的抱怨。类似的标题不断涌现，指责网络及其衍生应用、社交媒体网站和在线游戏让我们沉迷于分心。

paragraphs.text: There's little doubt that nearly everyone who comes in contact with the Net has difficulty disconnecting. Many of us, like Schwartz, struggle to stay focused on tasks that require more concentration than it takes to post a status update. As one person ironically put it in the comments section of Schwartz's online article, "As I was reading this very excellent article. I stopped at least half a dozen times to check my email."
paragraphs.translation: 毫无疑问，几乎所有接触网络的人都难以断开连接。我们中的许多人，像施瓦茨一样，难以保持专注在需要比发布状态更新更多集中力的任务上。正如有人在施瓦茨在线文章的评论区讽刺地说道：“我在阅读这篇非常优秀的文章时，至少停了六七次去查看我的电子邮件。”

paragraphs.text: There's something different about this technology: it is both invasive and persuasive. But who's at fault for its overuse? To find solutions, it's important to understand what we're dealing with. There are four parties conspiring to keep you connected: the tech, your boss, your friends and you.
paragraphs.translation: 这项技术有所不同：它既具有侵入性又具有说服力。但谁该为其过度使用负责？要找到解决方案，重要的是理解我们面对的是什么。有四方在共同作用让你保持连接：技术、你的老板、你的朋友和你自己。

paragraphs.text: The technologies themselves, and their makers, are the easiest suspects to blame for our diminishing attention spans. Nicholas Carr, author of The Shallows: What the Internet Is Doing to Our Brains, wrote, "The net is designed to be an interruption system, a machine geared to dividing attention."
paragraphs.translation: 技术本身及其制造者，是我们注意力 span 减少的最容易指责的对象。《浅薄：互联网如何毒化了我们的大脑》一书的作者尼古拉斯·卡尔写道：“网络被设计成一个中断系统，一台专门用于分散注意力的机器。”

paragraphs.text: Online services like Facebook, Twitter and the like, are called out of manipulation—making products so good that people can't stop using them. After studying these products for several years, I wrote a book about how they do it. I learned it all starts with the business model. Since these services rely on advertising revenue, the more frequently you use them, the more money they make. It's no wonder these companies employ teams of people focused on engineering their services to be as engaging as possible. These products aren't habit-forming by chance; it's by design. They have an incentive to keep us hooked.
paragraphs.translation: 像Facebook、Twitter等在线服务被指责在操纵——将产品做得如此之好，以至于人们无法停止使用它们。研究这些产品多年后，我写了一本书，讲述了他们是如何做到的。我了解到这一切都始于商业模式。由于这些服务依赖于广告收入，你使用得越频繁，他们赚的钱就越多。难怪这些公司雇佣团队专注于设计他们的服务，使其尽可能吸引人。这些产品不是偶然形成习惯的；这是设计使然。他们有动机让我们上瘾。

paragraphs.text: However, as good as these services are, there are simple steps we can take to keep them at bay. For example, we can change how often we receive the distracting notifications that trigger our urge to check. According to Adam Marchick, CEO of mobile marketing company Kahuna, less than 15 percent of smartphone users ever bother to adjust their notification settings--meaning the remaining 85 percent of us default to the app makers' every preset trigger. Google and Apple have made it far too difficult to adjust these settings so it's up to us to take steps to ensure we set these triggers to suit our own needs, not the needs of the app makers'.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，尽管这些服务很好，但我们可以采取简单措施来控制它们。例如，我们可以改变接收分散注意力的通知的频率，这些通知会触发我们查看的冲动。根据移动营销公司Kahuna的首席执行官Adam Marchick的说法，不到15%的智能手机用户会费心调整他们的通知设置——这意味着剩下的85%的人默认应用制造商的每一个预设触发器。Google和Apple使调整这些设置变得过于困难，因此我们必须采取措施，确保我们设置这些触发器以满足我们自己的需求，而不是应用制造商的需求。

paragraphs.text: While companies like Facebook harvest attention to generate revenue from advertisers, other technologies have no such agenda. Take email, for example. This system couldn't care less how often you use it. Yet to many, email is the most habit-forming medium of all. We check email at all hours of the day—we're obsessed, But why? Because that's what the boss wants. For almost all white-collar jobs, email is the primary tool of corporate communication. A slow response to a message could hurt not only your reputation but also your livelihood.
paragraphs.translation: 虽然像Facebook这样的公司通过收割注意力从广告商那里产生收入，但其他技术没有这样的议程。以电子邮件为例。这个系统根本不在乎你使用它的频率。然而，对许多人来说，电子邮件是最容易形成习惯的媒介。我们一天到晚都在查看电子邮件——我们沉迷其中。但为什么？因为那是老板想要的。对于几乎所有白领工作来说，电子邮件是公司沟通的主要工具。对消息的慢速响应不仅会损害你的声誉，还会损害你的生计。

paragraphs.text: Your friends are also responsible. Think about this familiar scene. People gathered around a table, enjoying food and each other's company. There's laughter and a bit of kidding. Then, during an interval in the conversation, someone takes out their phone to check who knows what. Barely anyone notices and no one says a thing.
paragraphs.translation: 你的朋友也有责任。想想这个熟悉的场景。人们围坐在桌旁，享受食物和彼此的陪伴。有笑声和一点玩笑。然后，在谈话的间隙，有人拿出手机查看什么。几乎没有人注意到，也没有人说一句话。

paragraphs.text: Now imagine the same dinner, but instead of checking their phone, the person belches (打嗝)-loudly. Everyone notices. Unless the meal takes place in a beer house, this is considered bad manners. The impolite act violates the basic rules of etiquette. One has to wonder: why don't we apply the same social norms to checking phones during meals, meetings and conversations as we do to other antisocial behaviors? Somehow, we accept it and say nothing when someone offends.
paragraphs.translation: 现在想象同样的晚餐，但不是查看手机，而是这个人打嗝——大声地。每个人都会注意到。除非用餐在啤酒馆进行，否则这被认为是不礼貌的。这种不礼貌的行为违反了基本的礼仪规则。人们不禁要问：为什么我们在用餐、会议和谈话中查看手机时，不应用与其他反社会行为相同的社会规范？不知何故，当有人冒犯时，我们接受它并一言不发。

paragraphs.text: The reality is taking one's phone out at the wrong time is worse than belching because, unlike other minor offense, checking tech is contagious. Once one person looks at their phone, other people feel compelled to do the same, starting a chain reaction. The more people are on their phones, the fewer people are talking until finally you are the only one left not reading email or checking Twitter. From a societal perspective, phone checking is less like belching in public and more like another bad habit. Our phones are like cigarettes-something to do when we're anxious, bored or when our fingers need something to toy with. Seeing others enjoy a smoke, or sneak a quick glance, is too tempting to resist and soon everyone is doing it.
paragraphs.translation: 现实是，在不恰当的时候拿出手机比打嗝更糟糕，因为与其他轻微冒犯不同，查看科技产品是会传染的。一旦一个人看手机，其他人会感到被迫做同样的事情，引发连锁反应。看手机的人越多，交谈的人就越少，直到最后只剩下你一个人不查看电子邮件或不刷Twitter。从社会的角度来看，查看手机不像在公共场合打嗝，而更像是另一种坏习惯。我们的手机就像香烟——当我们焦虑、无聊或手指需要玩点什么时可以做点事。看到别人享受抽烟，或偷偷瞥一眼，太诱人难以抗拒，很快每个人都在这样做。

paragraphs.text: The technology, your boss, and your friends, all influence how often you find yourself using (or overusing) these gadgets. But there's still someone who deserves scrutiny--the person holding the phone.
paragraphs.translation: 技术、你的老板和你的朋友，都影响着你使用（或过度使用）这些小工具的频率。但还有一个人值得审视——拿着手机的人。

paragraphs.text: I have a confession. Even though I study habit-forming technology for a living, disconnecting is not easy for me. I'm online far more than I'd like. Like Schwartz and so many others, I often find myself distracted and off tack. I wanted to know why so I began self-monitoring to try to understand my behavior. That's when I discovered an uncomfortable truth. I use technology as an escape. When I'm doing something I'd rather not do, or when I'm someplace I'd rather not be, I use my phone to port myself elsewhere. I found that this ability to instantly shift my attention was often a good thing, like when passing time on public transportation, but frequently my tech use was not so benign. When I faced difficult work, like thinking through an article idea or editing the same draft for the hundredth time, for example, a more sinister screen would draw me in. I could easily escape discomfort. temporarily. by answering email or browsing the web under the pretense of so-called "research." Though I desperately wanted to lay blame elsewhere, I finally had to admit that my bad habits had less to do with new-age. technology and more to do with old-fashioned procrastination (拖延).
paragraphs.translation: 我有个坦白。尽管我以研究习惯形成技术为生，但断开连接对我来说并不容易。我上网的时间远超我想要的。像施瓦茨和许多其他人一样，我经常发现自己分心和偏离正轨。我想知道为什么，所以我开始自我监控，试图理解我的行为。那时我发现了一个令人不安的真相。我使用技术作为一种逃避。当我在做我不愿意做的事情，或者当我在我不愿意去的地方时，我用手机将自己转移到别处。我发现这种瞬间转移注意力的能力通常是一件好事，比如在公共交通上消磨时间时，但我的技术使用往往并非如此良性。当我面对困难的工作时，比如思考文章想法或第一百次编辑同一篇草稿，一个更险恶的屏幕会吸引我。我可以轻易地暂时逃避不适，通过回答电子邮件或在所谓的“研究”名义下浏览网页。尽管我拼命想把责任推到别处，但我最终不得不承认，我的坏习惯与新时代技术关系不大，而更多与老式的拖延有关。

paragraphs.text: It's easy to blame technology for being so distracting, but distraction is nothing new. Aristotle and Socrates debated the nature of "akrasia"--our tendency to do things against our interests. If we're honest with ourselves, tech is just another way to occupy our time and minds, If we weren't on our devices. We'd likely do similarly unproductive.
paragraphs.translation: 很容易责怪技术如此分散注意力，但分心并不是什么新鲜事。亚里士多德和苏格拉底辩论过“akrasia”的本质——我们做违背自己利益的事情的倾向。如果我们对自己诚实，技术只是占据我们时间和思想的另一种方式，如果我们不在设备上，我们可能也会做同样无益的事情。

paragraphs.text: Personal technology is indeed more engaging than ever, and there's no doubt companies are engineering their products and services to be more compelling and attractive. But would we want it any other way? The intended result of making something better is that people use it more. That's not necessarily a problem, that's progress.
paragraphs.translation: 个人技术确实比以往任何时候都更吸引人，毫无疑问，公司正在设计他们的产品和服务，使其更具吸引力和诱惑力。但我们希望它变成另一种方式吗？使某物更好的预期结果是人们更多地使用它。这不一定是问题，这是进步。

paragraphs.text: These improvements don't mean we shouldn't attempt to control our use of technology. In order to make sure it doesn't control us, we should come to terms with the fact that it's more than the technology itself that's responsible for our habits. Our workplace culture, social norms and individual behaviors all play a part. To put technology in its place, we must be conscious not only of how technology is changing, but also of how it is changing us.
paragraphs.translation: 这些改进并不意味着我们不应该尝试控制我们对技术的使用。为了确保它不控制我们，我们应该接受这样一个事实：对我们的习惯负责的不仅仅是技术本身。我们的工作场所文化、社会规范和个人行为都起着作用。要使技术处于其适当位置，我们必须意识到技术如何变化，以及它如何改变我们。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: You may have heard that Coca-Cola once contained an ingredient capable of sparking particular devotion in consumers: cocaine. The cocaine. The "coca" in the name referred to the extracts of coca leaf that the drink's originator, chemist John Pemberton, mixed with his sugary syrup (浆汁). At the time, coca leaf extract mixed with wine was a common tonic (滋补品), and Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol. But the other half of the name represents another ingredient, less infamous (名声不好的), perhaps, but also strangely potent: the kola nut.
paragraphs.translation: 你可能听说过可口可乐曾经含有一种能引发消费者特别忠诚的成分：可卡因。正是可卡因。名称中的“可”指的是可口叶提取物，饮料的创始人、化学家约翰·彭伯顿将其与他的糖浆混合。当时，可口叶提取物与葡萄酒混合是一种常见的滋补品，而彭伯顿的甜酿则是绕过当地禁止销售酒精的法律的一种方式。但名称的另一半代表另一种成分，可能名声不那么差，但同样具有奇特功效：可乐果。

paragraphs.text: In West Africa, people have long chewed kola nuts as stimulants, because they contain caffeine that also occurs naturally in tea, coffee, and chocolate. They also have heart stimulants.
paragraphs.translation: 在西非，人们长期以来咀嚼可乐果作为兴奋剂，因为它们含有咖啡因，这种物质也自然存在于茶、咖啡和巧克力中。它们还具有心脏兴奋作用。

paragraphs.text: Historian Paul Lovejoy relates that the cultivation of kola nuts in West Africa is hundreds of years old. The leafy, spreading trees were planted on graves and as part of traditional rituals. Even though the nuts, which need to stay moist, can be somewhat delicate to transport, traders carried them hundreds of miles throughout the forests and grasslands.
paragraphs.translation: 历史学家保罗·洛夫乔伊指出，西非的可乐果种植已有数百年历史。这种枝叶繁茂的树木被种植在坟墓上，并作为传统仪式的一部分。尽管这些需要保持湿润的果实在运输上可能有些脆弱，但商人们还是将它们运送到数百英里外的森林和草原中。

paragraphs.text: Europeans did not know of them until the 1500s when Portuguese ships arrived on the coast of what is now Sierra Leone. And while the Portuguese took part in the trade, ferrying nuts down the coast along with other goods, by 1620, when English explorer Richard Jobson made his way up the Gambia, the nuts were still peculiar to his eyes.
paragraphs.translation: 欧洲人直到16世纪葡萄牙船只抵达现今塞拉利昂海岸时才知道它们。尽管葡萄牙人参与了贸易，将果实与其他货物一起沿岸运输，但到1620年，当英国探险家理查德·乔布森前往冈比亚时，这些果实在他眼中仍然很奇特。

paragraphs.text: By the late 19th century, kola nuts were being shipped by the tonne to Europe and the US. Many made their way into medicines, intended as a kind of energy boost. One such popular medicinal drink was Vin Mariani, a French product consisting of coca extract mixed with red wine. It was created by a French chemist, Angelo Mariani, in 1863. So when Pemberton created his drink, it represented an ongoing trend. When cocaine eventually fell from grace as a beverage ingredient, kola-extract colas became popular.
paragraphs.translation: 到19世纪末，可乐果被成吨地运往欧洲和美国。许多被制成药物，旨在作为一种能量增强剂。其中一种流行的药用饮料是马里亚尼酒，这是一种法国产品，由可口提取物与红葡萄酒混合而成。它由法国化学家安杰洛·马里亚尼于1863年创造。因此，当彭伯顿创造他的饮料时，它代表了一种持续的趋势。当可卡因最终不再作为饮料成分受欢迎时，可乐提取物可乐变得流行。

paragraphs.text: The first year it was available, Coca-Cola averaged nine servings a day across all the Atlanta soda fountains where it was sold. As it grew more popular, the company sold rights to bottle the soda, so it could travel easily. Today about 1.9 billion Cokes are purchased daily. It's become so iconic that attempts to change its taste in 1985-sweetening it in a move projected to boost sales proved disastrous, with widespread anger from consumers. "Coca-Cola Classic" returned to store shelves just three months after the "New Coke" was released.
paragraphs.translation: 在它上市的第一年，可口可乐在亚特兰大所有销售它的汽水平均每天售出九份。随着它越来越受欢迎，公司出售了瓶装汽水的权利，以便于运输。如今，每天大约购买19亿瓶可口可乐。它变得如此标志性，以至于1985年试图改变其口味——通过增加甜度来预计提升销售——结果证明是灾难性的，引发了消费者的广泛愤怒。“可口可乐经典”在“新可乐”发布仅三个月后就重新回到商店货架。

paragraphs.text: These days, the Coca-Cola recipe is a closely guarded secret. But it's said to no longer contain kola nut extract, relying instead on artificial imitations to achieve the flavour.
paragraphs.translation: 如今，可口可乐的配方是一个严格保守的秘密。但据说它不再含有可乐果提取物，而是依赖人工仿制品来达到其风味。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Twenty years ago, the Urban Land Institute defined the two types of cities that dominated the US landscape: smaller cities that operated around standard 9-5 business hours and large metropolitan areas that ran all 24 hours of the day. Analyzing and comparing cities using the lens of this basic divide gives interesting context to how investment capital flows and housing prices have shifted.
paragraphs.translation: 二十年前，城市土地协会定义了主导美国城市格局的两类城市：一类是遵循标准朝九晚五营业时间的较小城市，另一类是全天24小时运转的大都市区。通过这种基本划分的视角来分析和比较城市，为投资资本流动和房价变动提供了有趣的背景。

paragraphs.text: In recent years, many mid-sized cities have begun to adopt a middle-of-the-road approach incorporating the excitement and opportunity of large cities with small cities' quiet after midnight. These 18-hour cities are beginning to make waves in real estate rankings and attract more real estate investment. What is underlying this new movement in real estate, and why do these cities have so much appeal?
paragraphs.translation: 近年来，许多中型城市开始采取折中方式，将大城市的活力与机遇同小城市午夜后的宁静相结合。这些18小时城市开始在房地产排名中崭露头角，并吸引更多房地产投资。这一房地产新运动背后的深层原因是什么？为何这些城市如此具有吸引力？

paragraphs.text: 18-hour cities combine the best of 24-hour and 9-5 cities, which contributes to downtown revitalization. For decades, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities were abandoned after work hours by workers who lived in the suburbs. Movement out of city centers was widespread, and downtown tenants were predominantly made up of the working poor. This generated little commerce for downtown businesses in the evenings, which made business and generating tax revenue for municipal upkeep difficult. With the rise of a new concept in urban planning that aims to make life easier and more convenient, increasing popularity for urban areas that caused the real estate pushes, in major cities like San Francisco or New York, has inspired a type of forward thinking urbanity and in smaller cities.
paragraphs.translation: 18小时城市融合了24小时城市和9-5城市的优点，从而促进了市中心的复兴。几十年来，许多小中型城市的市中心核心区在下班后被居住在郊区的工作者所抛弃。人口流出市中心的现象十分普遍，市中心的租户主要是贫困劳动者。这导致市中心商户在傍晚时段几乎没有商业活动，使得企业经营和为市政维护筹集税收变得困难。随着旨在使生活更便捷的新城市规划理念兴起，大城市如旧金山或纽约中日益受欢迎的城市区域推动了房地产发展，这也启发了小城市出现一种前瞻性的都市化思维。

paragraphs.text: Transforming downtown areas so that they incorporate modern housing and improved walkability to local restaurants, retail, and entertainment -especially when combined with improved infrastructure for cyclists and public transit-makes them appeal to a more affluent demographic. These adjustments encourage employers in the knowledge and talent industries to keep their offices downtown. Access to foot traffic and proximity to transit allow the type of entertainment-oriented businesses such as bars and restaurants to stay open later, which attracts both younger, creative workers and baby boomers nearing retirement alike. Because of their smaller size, most keep hours that allow people to enjoy themselves, then have some quiet after midnight, as opposed to large major cities like New York, where the buzz of activity is ongoing.
paragraphs.translation: 改造市中心，使其融入现代住房和改善通往本地餐厅、零售及娱乐场所的步行便利性——尤其是结合改善后的自行车和公共交通基础设施——能让这些区域吸引更富裕的人群。这些调整鼓励知识型和人才密集型行业的雇主将其办公室设在市中心。人流量和靠近交通枢纽的优势，使得酒吧和餐馆等娱乐导向型企业能够延长营业时间，这既吸引了年轻的创意工作者，也吸引了临近退休的婴儿潮一代。由于规模较小，大多数这些城市的营业时间允许人们享受生活，然后在午夜后归于宁静，而不像纽约这样的大都市，喧嚣的活动持续不断。

paragraphs.text: These 18-hour cities are rapidly on the rise and offer great opportunities for homeowner investment. In many of these cities such as Denver, a diverse and vigorous economy attracted to the urban core has offered stable employment for residents. The right urban mix has propped up home occupancy, increased property values, and attracted significant investment capital.
paragraphs.translation: 这些18小时城市正在迅速崛起，并为业主投资提供了巨大机会。在丹佛等许多此类城市中，多样化且充满活力的经济吸引了核心城区，为居民提供了稳定的就业机会。恰当的城市组合支撑了房屋入住率，提升了房产价值，并吸引了大量投资资本。

questionGroups.sourceText: 太湖是中国东部的一个淡水湖,占地面积2250平方公里,是中国第三大淡水湖,仅次于鄱阳和洞庭。太湖约有90个岛屿,大小从几平方米到几平方公里不等。太湖以其独特的"太湖石"而闻名,太湖石常用于装饰中国传统园林。太湖也以高产的捕鱼业闻名。自上世纪70年代后期以来,捕捞鱼蟹对沿湖的居民来说极为重要,并对周边地区的经济作出了重大贡献。太湖地区是中国陶瓷(ceramics)业基地之一,其中宜兴的陶瓷厂家生产举世闻名的宜兴紫砂壶(clay teapot)。

answer.modelTranslation: Taihu Lake, located in eastern China, covers an area of 2250 square kilometers and is the third largest freshwater lake in China, following Poyang and Dongting. The lake is home to about 90 islands, ranging in size from several square meters to several square kilometers. Taihu is renowned for its unique 'Taihu stones', which are commonly used to decorate traditional Chinese gardens. The lake is also famous for its abundant fishing industry. Since the late 1970s, fishing for fish and crabs has been extremely important for residents along the lake and has made significant contributions to the economy of the surrounding areas. The Taihu region is one of the bases of China's ceramics industry, with Yixing's ceramic manufacturers producing the world-renowned Yixing purple sand teapots.
